correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 with symmetric positive undirected edges, no loops, minimum support-degree at least two, connected nonbipartite B, the exact complete-layer identity A=P-(I-P)/(n-1) yields C_k=(1-t_k)P+t_kB and strict positivity. Solving the stationary equation gives nu_k=(1-t)u(I-tB)^-1. Reversible spectral decomposition in L2(pi) gives nu_k/pi=1+sum_j a_j(1-t)/(1-t lambda_j)e_j, with derivative (lambda_j-1)/(1-t lambda_j)^2 strictly negative. Orthogonality proves chi-square parity inequalities; taking x_i=d_min/d_i gives the strict scalar consensus law. On the quotient by constants the eigenvalues are exactly t lambda_j; the loopless trace and equality characterization prove strict monotone per-time-step rate for irregular B. Exact-fraction replay passed on four graphs and twelve periods each; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The primary Shiu–Naghizadeh 2026 source Section IV-A has one three-agent, k=1 noninterpolation example, and IV-B/IV-C give a generic SLEM upper bound and an asymptotic O-bound. Neither the read Sections II-D and IV-A–IV-C nor the related checked abstracts gave the all-graph strict chi-square parity interlacing, the bounded inverse-degree consensus witness at every odd k, or exact complete-layer SLEM with strict time-normalized monotonicity. Scope matches the earlier 2025 model, not the later mere revision date. This is a best-knowledge originality decision subject to the full-2025-paper and broader-resolvent risks.
residual_risks: The 2025 proceedings version is an earlier treatment of switching and was accessible only through its dated abstract; unseen full text could have stronger results than the 2026 complete openly readable version.

Generic results on Markov-chain resolvents, signed teleportation, or chi-square comparisons might imply the universal parity statement without the same wording; no decisive equivalence was found in the inspected sources.

The theorem is a strict all-graph result only within a complete-loopless first layer and a reversible, connected, nonbipartite, support-degree-at-least-two second layer. It does not assert novel Markov spectral techniques or claims for arbitrary opinions.

value.rationale: The source gives a single noninterpolating switching example and general stability/rate estimates but leaves the topology-independent sign and switching-period mechanism unspecified. This theorem determines an exact, robust all-irregular-graph parity phase ordering for a natural invariant of social influence, chi-square disparity relative to degree-weighted influence, and supplies a canonical bounded anti-hub opinion whose consensus overshoots both isolated contexts at every odd period. This is a structural, falsifiable generalization across all n, weights, and switching lengths, not an arbitrary single-parameter re-computation. The exact contraction spectrum additionally distinguishes rate monotonicity from consensus-value oscillation. No claims for directed layers, generic opinions, or stochastic-agent behavior.
